elements.evidence: Both included registrations name amyloid cardiomyopathy. The limb does real work at screening: ATTR POLYNEUROPATHY trials share the same drugs and are a different disease in a different population, and were excluded on this ground.
Matched against the declared synonym set -- tafamidis, vyndaqel, vyndamax, FX-1006A, PF-06291826, acoramidis, AG10, attruby.

Both included trials declare a placebo arm. THE LIMB CARRIES MOST OF THE EXCLUSIONS: only 6 of the 46 screened remainder trials declare a placebo arm at all -- this drug programme is dominated by open-label extension and single-arm studies.

elements.criterion: a hierarchical composite analysed by win ratio -- AND the SAME hierarchy
elements.evidence_and_why_it_does_not_settle: THIS IS THE LIMB THAT DECIDES THE TOPIC AND NO FIELD SETTLES IT. Both included trials pass 'hierarchical win ratio' -- and they still cannot be combined, because ATTR-ACT's hierarchy is mortality plus CV hospitalisation (2 tiers) while ATTRibute-CM's adds NT-proBNP and 6-minute-walk change (4 tiers). A win ratio's estimand IS its hierarchy. Comparing two hierarchies for identity is a READING of two verbatim strings, not a field lookup, so it is recorded as DERIVED. TWO DIFFERENT HIERARCHIES ARE TWO ESTIMANDS, NOT HETEROGENEITY.

primary.outcome_definition: Hierarchical Combination of All-Cause Mortality and Frequency of Cardiovascular-Related Hospitalizations

outcome_definition_source.description_verbatim: All-cause mortality and frequency of cardiovascular hospitalization were analyzed using Finkelstein-Schoenfeld method. The method combines all-cause mortality and frequency of CV-related hospitalizations in a hierarchical fashion using all-cause mortality first. The method compares every participant with every other participant within strata, assigning a +1 to the "better" participant and a -1 to the "worse" participant and 0 if they are "tied". Participants who discontinued for transplantation (heart transplantation and combined heart and liver transplantation) or for implantation of a cardiac mechanical assist device, were handled in the same manner as death. 'Win' represents a participant doing better based on hierarchical comparison. The reported unit is the total "wins" for each treatment group from performing such a hierarchical comparison across all 4 strata in the study.
outcome_definition_source.components_as_the_registry_states_them: a HIERARCHICAL COMBINATION of ALL-CAUSE MORTALITY and FREQUENCY OF CARDIOVASCULAR-RELATED HOSPITALIZATIONS. Two levels, analysed by win ratio -- every patient is compared with every other and the result is a ratio of wins to losses, not a count of events over a denominator.
outcome_definition_source.analysis_set_as_the_registry_states_it: 30 months. Arm sizes here are 264 against 177, which is the pooled tafamidis doses against placebo.

outcome_definition_source.description_verbatim: The endpoint was analyzed using Finkelstein-Schoenfeld method. The method combines all-cause mortality, cumulative frequency of CV-related hospitalizations, change from baseline in NT-proBNP and change from baseline in 6MWT in a hierarchical fashion. The method compares every participant with every other participant within strata, assigning a +1 to the "better" participant and a -1 to the "worse" participant and 0 if they are "tied". Participants who had heart transplantation or implantation of a cardiac mechanical assist device were handled in the same manner as death. 'Win' represents a participant doing better based on hierarchical comparison. The reported unit is the total percent of "wins" for each treatment group from performing such a hierarchical comparison across stratification factors in the study.

FOUR levels, and the lower two are CONTINUOUS change scores, not events at all.

primary.poolable_reason: BOTH TRIALS REGISTER HIERARCHICAL ENDPOINTS ANALYSED BY WIN RATIO, AND A WIN RATIO CANNOT BE RECOVERED FROM A 2x2 TABLE. ATTR-ACT's registered primary, verbatim, is a 'Hierarchical Combination of All-Cause Mortality and Frequency of Cardiovascular-Related Hospitalizations'. In such an analysis every patient in one arm is compared with every patient in the other and the result is a ratio of wins to losses; there is no numerator over a denominator to extract, and reducing it to counts of participants discards the hierarchy that defines it. AND THE TWO HIERARCHIES ARE NOT THE SAME HIERARCHY. ATTRibute-CM's registered primary is a 'Hierarchical Combination of All-Cause Mortality, Cumulative Frequency of CV-related Hospitalization, CHANGE FROM BASELINE IN NT-proBNP and CHANGE FROM BASELINE IN 6MWT'. That is FOUR levels to ATTR-ACT's two, and its lower two levels are CONTINUOUS CHANGE SCORES rather than events. Two hierarchies of different depth, whose tie-breaking rules differ and whose lower levels are not even the same kind of quantity, do not estimate one thing.

pooled.withdrawn_note: WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: NOT that tafamidis or acoramidis is ineffective in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy. The trials here measure hierarchical win-ratio composites of death, hospitalisation and functional change, and nothing on this page estimates the question its title implies. WHAT IS CONFIRMED: the original withdrawal was RIGHT and its one-line reason -- 'win-ratio composite reduced to 2x2 counts' -- is exactly the defect, now sourced from both registrations. Both identities are correct. RE-VERIFICATION ADDED the second, independent ground the original did not name: the two hierarchies differ in depth and in kind. THE REPLACEMENT QUESTION IS PARKED: a synthesis of win ratios is possible in principle but requires each trial's own win-ratio estimate and its variance, which the registry's protocol record does not carry.
pooled.reverification: RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-18. VERDICT: CONFIRMED and SHARPENED. The stated reason survives verbatim; re-verification added that ATTRibute-CM's hierarchy has four levels to ATTR-ACT's two, and that its lower two are continuous change scores -- so even a correct win-ratio synthesis would not be comparing like with like.

primary.poolable_DEPRECATED_note: `poolable` MEANT ONLY 'the source page pooled these trials'. It was never a judgement that the pool was sound, and the renderer read it as permission to assert 'pooled on the X scale'. RENAMED to source_page_pooled, which is what it says. `poolable` is retained so nothing breaks, and it is DEPRECATED: read source_page_pooled for what the source did, and estimand_established for whether the pool is defensible. A PAGE SHOULD DISPLAY A POOLED ESTIMATE BECAUSE ITS ESTIMAND WAS ESTABLISHED, NOT BECAUSE SOMEONE ONCE POOLED IT.
primary.estimand_established_means: TRUE only where every contributing trial has been READ and shown to measure the same quantity, or the same construct with a variance stated. FALSE where that was checked and failed. NULL where it was never checked -- AN ABSENT ASSERTION AND A NEGATIVE ONE ARE DIFFERENT STATES and null is not a pass.

manuscript.introduction:
This review asks: Both trials register HIERARCHICAL endpoints analysed by win ratio, and the two hierarchies are not the same hierarchy.

It examines 2 randomised trials and DOES NOT POOL THEM, against placebo.

The outcome sought is Hierarchical composites, analysed by win ratio -- and the two hierarchies differ.

remainder_dispositions.what_this_says: READ BY THE REMAINDER-DIAGNOSIS RULE: 31 of 46 fail a criterion, and the dominant ground is COMPARATOR -- only 6 of the 46 declare a placebo arm at all. This is a drug programme dominated by OPEN-LABEL EXTENSION and single-arm studies, so the query is well aimed and the randomised evidence is genuinely thin. Neither the too-broad-query shape nor the fragmented-estimand shape: a third reading, where the field itself has produced few controlled trials.
remainder_dispositions.no_poolable_candidates: ZERO trials in the remainder are eligible AND poolable -- unlike alirocumab-lipid, where screening recovered two. Stated explicitly because a zero here is a real result about this evidence base rather than an absence of effort.

k_cascade.why_k_included_is_2_and_stays_2: THE POOLING OBSTACLE IS THE ESTIMAND, NOT THE EVIDENCE BASE. Both included trials register HIERARCHICAL endpoints analysed by win ratio, and the two hierarchies are not the same hierarchy: ATTR-ACT combines all-cause mortality with CV-related hospitalisation frequency (2 tiers); ATTRibute-CM adds NT-proBNP change and 6-minute-walk change (4 tiers). Verified from the registry 2026-08-19. A win ratio's estimand IS its hierarchy and cannot be recovered from a 2x2 table. TWO DIFFERENT HIERARCHIES ARE TWO ESTIMANDS, NOT HETEROGENEITY -- so k=2 is the count of included trials and NOT a pooled k.
k_cascade._why: k is never one number. Each stage is what the instrument at that stage could actually decide.
k_cascade.regated_2026_08_19_trailing_placebo: THE ONLY ONE OF THE FIVE GATED TOPICS WHOSE CASCADE DID NOT MOVE. Re-run against the repaired classifier with the old code loaded from git at 7a08bcbe1 and the surfaced set re-executed (55 today, 55 stored): ZERO of the 55 records changed role. Recorded as a measured null rather than left silent, because 'unchanged' and 'not checked' look identical on a finished page. k2_role_located was separately corrected from 55 to 52 -- an arithmetic defect in the stage label, not a movement. risk_of_bias.tool: RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials)
risk_of_bias.version: 22 August 2019 version, as reproduced in the Cochrane Handbook
risk_of_bias.handbook: Higgins JPT, Savovic J, Page MJ, Elbers RG, Sterne JAC. Chapter 8: Assessing risk of bias in a randomized trial. In: Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions version 6.5.1
risk_of_bias.unit_of_assessment: A RESULT, not a study -- Handbook 8.2: 'risk of bias is assessed for a specific result'. Every judgement below names its outcome.
risk_of_bias.default_rule: A domain that cannot be judged from the registration and the published report is NO_INFORMATION, never LOW. Low-by-default asserts a fact; high-by-default invents a defect.

ceiling.statement: NO RESULT IN THIS REVIEW CAN REACH LOW RISK OF BIAS ON THE EVIDENCE WE CAN REACH, AND THAT IS A FACT ABOUT OUR ACCESS RATHER THAN ABOUT THE TRIALS. The two domains that would distinguish LOW from SOME CONCERNS need documents this review does not hold: D1 needs allocation concealment and baseline data, which are in neither the registration nor the published abstract; D5 needs the trial's statistical analysis plan, which is not held for any trial. SOME CONCERNS IS THEREFORE THE CEILING, NOT A FINDING. A trial rated SOME CONCERNS here may well be at low risk of bias -- we cannot show it, and we do not imply the opposite.
ceiling.what_would_change_it: Retrieving each trial's full published report and its statistical analysis plan or protocol. Until then the rating is bounded by what we read, and the bound is reported rather than the reader inferring it.
ceiling.why_this_is_stated_rather_than_left_impl: A rating of SOME CONCERNS with no explanation reads as a judgement against the trial. Omitting the reason would manufacture a criticism exactly as a low-by-default manufactures a reassurance -- the same defect pointed the other way.

evidence: Allocation concealment and baseline-imbalance data are in neither the registration nor the fields this object holds.

Cochrane Handbook 6.5.1 section 8.7 scopes domain 5 to selective reporting BY THE TRIAL AUTHORS; selection performed by a review in assembling its synthesis is a review-level matter and RoB 2 has no domain for it, because the tool assesses trials and not reviews. d5_scope_rule.position: DOMAIN 5 ASSESSES THE TRIAL'S SELECTION AMONG ITS OWN RESULTS, NOT THIS REVIEW'S SELECTION AMONG THE TRIAL'S REPORTED RESULTS. Cochrane Handbook 6.5.1 section 8.7 scopes domain 5 to selective reporting BY THE TRIAL AUTHORS; selection performed by a review in assembling its synthesis is a review-level matter and RoB 2 has no domain for it, because the tool assesses trials and not reviews. This review's own selection among the results a trial reported is therefore DECLARED beside the estimate and is NOT folded into any domain judgement. Folding it in would record a property of this review as though it were a property of the trial, which is a factual error about the trial in the accusing direction.
d5_scope_rule.review_level_selection_goes_to: Chapter 13 (assessing risk of bias due to missing results in a synthesis) for the synthesis-level question, and to an explicit DECLARATION beside each affected estimate for the per-result question, which is `our_selection_declared_not_rated` on every record below.
d5_scope_rule.position_withdrawn: An earlier version of this function implemented the opposite position WITHOUT DECLARING IT: it set signalling question 5.2 to PROBABLY_YES whenever the result used here sat at SECONDARY or OTHER rank, on the ground that the rank was chosen by this review -- while stating in its own evidence text that the selection was 'the reviewers', not the trialists''. That is question 5.2 answered about the reviewers and then attributed to the trial. It reached 4 stored records, all in `iv-iron-hf`, and reached ZERO bytes of any delivered page. It is withdrawn here, and the withdrawal is recorded rather than the code quietly changing under an unchanged docstring.
d5_scope_rule.decided_by: Mahmood, 2026-08-24, on escalation E1 from the RoB 2 lane.

rob2_rederivation_2026_08_26.handbook: Cochrane Handbook v6.5 section 8.2.3: the domain-level judgements are Low / Some concerns / High; "No information" is one of the five signalling-question responses.

grade.reference: Schunemann H, Brozek J, Guyatt G, Oxman A (editors). GRADE Handbook for grading quality of evidence and strength of recommendations.
grade.handbook_chapter: Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions version 6.5.1, Chapter 14: Completing 'Summary of findings' tables and grading the certainty of the evidence
grade.starting_point: HIGH for a body of randomised evidence, then rated down with reasons.
grade.not_rated_up: No domain is rated UP. Rating up for large effect or dose-response applies to observational evidence that has not already been rated down, and neither condition holds here.

primary.why_not: This pool is declined or withdrawn, so there is no effect estimate to rate the certainty OF. Rating it would be certainty about a number this review refused to publish. The reason for the refusal is on the object.

protocol.why: A protocol specified before data collection is a HISTORICAL FACT ABOUT THE PAST and cannot be created retrospectively. Writing one now and calling it prespecified would invalidate every other refusal on these pages, because a reader who caught it would be right to disbelieve all of them.
protocol.what_was_actually_done: Eligibility criteria were derived POST HOC from the trials and the methodological authority, and the derivation is recorded element by element in `screening.eligibility_provenance` with the source of each.
protocol.authority_permitting_it: MECIR R107 permits post-hoc eligibility criteria PROVIDED THEY ARE DECLARED AS SUCH. They are declared, here and on the page, and the page says 'derived, post hoc' in its heading.
protocol.forward_remedy: For topics not yet built, a protocol is to be written and registered BEFORE the search is executed, so that the claim becomes true GOING FORWARD. It is never to be made true retroactively for a built topic.

bookkeeping_2026_08_21._what: The five reporting claims a PRISMA-2020 manuscript needs that are FETCHABLE rather than argued -- each derived from a field here, or stated as an honest absence.
bookkeeping_2026_08_21.which_limbs_this_review_refuses: Of the four properties this project requires of a completed topic, 1 are held (rob per result) and 3 are refused with the obstacle named in the evidence (comparison denominator, grade per pool, model output verbatim).
bookkeeping_2026_08_21.the_search_its_date_and_its_databases: PRIMARY TRIALS. NO BIBLIOGRAPHIC SEARCH FOR PRIMARY TRIALS WAS RUN. The 2 included trials were identified by reading named registrations on the dates recorded on each entry. This object's verification rests on ClinicalTrials.gov protocol records, read 2026-08-18. This review does not claim that any per-trial count was checked against a results record. The bar this object had to clear is not recorded.
bookkeeping_2026_08_21.whether_this_review_was_prospectively_re: NO PROSPERO REGISTRATION OR PROTOCOL RECORD IS HELD ON THIS OBJECT. That is not the same as knowing this review was not registered, and neither claim is made. It is recorded here as an absence so that a reader does not have to infer it from silence.
bookkeeping_2026_08_21.that_two_assessors_disagreed_and_where: Risk of bias was assessed independently a second time by GPT-5 Codex (openai family), via `codex exec`, blind to this assessment and given the same registry facts. 4 of 12 judgements -- 33.3%. Reported as DISAGREEMENT: agreement between two assessors given the same facts authenticates nothing. By domain: D1 0 of 2 disagree, D2 0 of 2 disagree, D3 0 of 2 disagree, D4 2 of 2 disagree, D5 2 of 2 disagree, OVERALL 0 of 2 disagree.
bookkeeping_2026_08_21.which_risk_of_bias_domains_drove_the_rat: Where a result is rated worse than LOW overall, the domain carrying that judgement is: D1 on 2 result(s), D2 on 2 result(s), D3 on 2 result(s), D5 on 2 result(s). The overall rating is the worst domain, so these are the domains that determine it.

trial_identity_check.method: the drug pattern from the matcher's own TOPICS list, compared against the registered arm structure

NCT03860935.why: no arm name matches the pattern, and arm names are paraphrases -- this method cannot decide identity for this trial

trial_identity_check.what_undecidable_means: The registered arm names do not name this intervention the way the review does, or the drug sits outside the experimental arm and registry arm-type labels are not reliable enough to judge on. It is NOT a pass and NOT a failure: this check could not decide, and no other check has looked.
